A typical anther is said to be dithecous because it
has two thecae joined by a connective
Dithecous means the bilobed anther has two thecae; the two thecae are joined by a sterile band called the connective, and each theca carries two microsporangia.
How many microsporangia are present in a typical angiosperm anther?
Each of the two thecae has two microsporangia located at its corners, so a typical anther has four microsporangia arranged longitudinally, two in each lobe.
bi- or multinucleate with dense cytoplasm
the outermost layer of the microsporangium
Because they carry out intense nutritive and secretory activity, tapetal cells have dense cytoplasm and generally contain more than one nucleus.
The proximal end of the filament of a stamen is normally attached to the
A stamen has a filament and a terminal anther; the proximal end of the filament is attached to the thalamus (receptacle) or to a petal of the flower.
The androecium of a flower, made up of stamens, is functionally the
The androecium is the male reproductive whorl of the flower, made up of stamens; the gynoecium, made up of pistils, is the female reproductive whorl.
The microsporangia of an anther run
The microsporangia run longitudinally along the anther, two in each of the two lobes, giving four microsporangia in all.
In transverse section, a young microsporangium is bounded by wall layers totalling
In transverse section a young microsporangium is surrounded by four wall layers: epidermis, endothecium, middle layers and tapetum.
The outer three wall layers of a microsporangium (epidermis, endothecium, middle layers) chiefly function in
protection and dehiscence of the anther
forming the exine of pollen grains
The outer three layers protect the microsporangium and bring about dehiscence of the anther to release pollen; only the innermost tapetum performs the nutritive function.
The centre of each microsporangium is occupied by a compact group of diploid cells called the
The sporogenous tissue is a compact, homogeneous group of diploid cells at the centre of the microsporangium; these cells become pollen mother cells and undergo meiosis.
A microsporangium, once mature, develops into a
pollen sac packed with pollen grains
Each microsporangium later develops into a pollen sac packed with pollen grains, which are released when the anther dehisces.
The number and length of stamens in a flower
is always exactly six across all angiosperms
is fixed at four for all dicots
is always equal to the number of petals
The number and length of stamens varies widely among different species of flowering plants; there is no fixed universal number.
The exine is the hard outer layer of the pollen wall and is made of sporopollenin, one of the most resistant organic materials known; the intine is made of cellulose…
In about 60 per cent of angiosperms, pollen grains are shed at the
In roughly 60% of angiosperms the generative cell divides into two male gametes before shedding, so the pollen grain is shed at the 3-celled stage.
Meiosis of a single pollen mother cell produces
a tetrad of four haploid microspores
a dyad of two haploid microspores
Each diploid pollen mother cell undergoes meiosis to produce a microspore tetrad, that is, four haploid microspores, each of which becomes a pollen grain.
For use in pollen banks, pollen grains of a large number of species are stored in
Pollen retains viability for years when stored in liquid nitrogen at –196°C; such pollen banks, like seed banks, are used in crop breeding programmes.
Pollen grains of which plant are a well-known cause of allergy, asthma and bronchitis in sensitive people?

A pollen grain, representing the male gametophyte, is generally
flat and disc-shaped, visible to the naked eye
The pollen grain, representing the male gametophyte, is generally spherical and measures about 25-50 micrometres in diameter.
The intine, the inner layer of the pollen wall, is composed of
The intine is a thin and continuous inner layer of the pollen wall made of cellulose and pectin, in contrast to the sporopollenin-based exine.
The stalk by which an ovule is attached to the placenta is called the
The funicle is the stalk of the ovule; the point where the funicle joins the body of the ovule is the hilum.
Michelia is an example of a gynoecium that is
In Michelia the many pistils of the gynoecium remain free from one another, which is the apocarpous condition; in Papaver the pistils are fused, that is syncarpous.
Megasporogenesis in an ovule results in the formation of
The diploid megaspore mother cell undergoes meiosis, passing through the dyad stage, and forms a megaspore tetrad of four haploid megaspores.
The basal region of the ovule, lying opposite to the micropylar end, is the
The chalaza is the basal part of the ovule opposite the micropyle; the hilum is the ovule’s junction with the funicle.
In an ovule, the embryo sac is located within the
The nucellus, enclosed by the integuments, has abundant reserve food and encloses the embryo sac (female gametophyte); usually one ovule has a single embryo sac.
The number of ovules in an ovary can vary from a single ovule, as in wheat and mango, to a very large number, as in
The ovary may contain a single ovule (wheat, paddy, mango) or a very large number of ovules (papaya, watermelon, orchids), each ovule attached to the placenta.
A flower whose gynoecium has more than one pistil is described as
A gynoecium with a single pistil is monocarpellary; with more than one pistil it is multicarpellary, which may be further syncarpous or apocarpous.
The integument(s) of an ovule cover the nucellus completely except for a small opening at the tip called the
The ovule is covered by one or two protective integuments which enclose it except at a small opening at the tip called the micropyle.
A mature angiosperm embryo sac is
There are 2 synergids, 1 egg, 3 antipodals and 1 central cell, making 7 cells; the central cell contains two polar nuclei, so the total number of nuclei is 8.
The filiform apparatus is a special thickening present in the
The synergids bear special cellular thickenings at their micropylar tip called the filiform apparatus, which guides the pollen tube into the synergid.
The two polar nuclei of the embryo sac are located in the
During cellularisation six nuclei are surrounded by walls; the remaining two, the polar nuclei, remain free in the large central cell.
The egg apparatus of a mature embryo sac consists of
one egg cell and three synergids
two synergids and one egg cell
two egg cells and one synergid
The three cells at the micropylar end form the egg apparatus, which is made up of two synergids and one egg cell.
After the 8-nucleate stage of the embryo sac, the process by which cell walls are laid down around six of the nuclei is called
Cellularisation is the process, following the 8-nucleate free-nuclear stage, in which cell walls are laid down, converting free nuclei into an organised embryo sac.
The three antipodal cells of the embryo sac are grouped at the
Three cells are grouped at the chalazal end and are called the antipodal cells, opposite to the egg apparatus at the micropylar end.
In most flowering plants, the megaspore that remains functional and develops into the embryo sac is usually the one at the
The functional megaspore, which alone survives and forms the embryo sac by successive mitotic divisions, is usually the one at the chalazal end of the tetrad.
The successive free-nuclear mitotic divisions of the functional megaspore give rise, in order, to embryo sacs with
The nucleus of the functional megaspore first divides to form a 2-nucleate embryo sac; two more successive mitoses give the 4-nucleate and then the 8-nucleate embryo…
Transfer of pollen grains from the anther of one flower to the stigma of another flower borne on the same plant is called
Geitonogamy involves two different flowers of the same plant. A pollinating agent is needed, but since the pollen is from the same plant it is genetically equivalent…
A large feathery stigma together with light, non-sticky pollen is an adaptation for
Wind-pollinated flowers have well-exposed stamens and a large feathery stigma to trap air-borne pollen; the pollen must be light and non-sticky so that it is carried…
Which plant genus shows an obligate mutualism with its pollinator moth, where the moth lays eggs in the ovary locule in return for pollination?
Yucca and the Yucca moth show obligate mutualism: the moth lays its eggs in the ovary locule and in return pollinates the flower; neither can complete its life cycle…

in the ovary, just before fertilisation
never; only one male gamete is produced
in the pollen tube, during its growth

In a hybridisation programme, emasculation can be omitted when
the female parent bears unisexual flowers
If the female parent produces unisexual flowers there are no anthers to remove, so the female flower bud is simply bagged before it opens and pollinated later with…
After the desired pollen has been dusted on a receptive, emasculated stigma, the final step in artificial hybridisation is to
repeat emasculation on the same flower
re-bag the flower and allow the fruit to develop
remove the stigma to stop further pollination
expose the flower to direct sunlight immediately
After pollination with the desired pollen, the flower is re-bagged and the fruit is allowed to develop, completing the standard sequence of emasculation, bagging,…

In a dicot embryo, the portion of the embryonal axis lying above the level of attachment of the cotyledons is the
The epicotyl lies above the level of cotyledon attachment and ends in the plumule (shoot tip); the hypocotyl lies below it and ends in the radicle, which is covered…
The two fusion events of double fertilisation, syngamy and triple fusion, occur
in two different embryo sacs of the same ovule
in the same embryo sac, at nearly the same time
in the anther, before pollination occurs
one in the style and one in the ovary

In a monocot (grass) embryo, the hollow sheath that encloses the shoot apex and leaf primordia is the
The epicotyl region of a grass embryo bears the shoot apex and leaf primordia, enclosed in a hollow foliar sheath called the coleoptile; the radicle is similarly…
the persistent endosperm of a mature seed
the persistent remnant of the nucellus
the hardened integument forming the seed coat
the outer wall of the fruit

Apple and strawberry are called false fruits because
their seeds are borne outside the fruit wall
the thalamus also contributes to the fruit
they develop only from the ovary
In a false fruit a floral part other than the ovary — usually the thalamus — contributes to the fruit. True fruits such as mango and tomato develop from the ovary alone.
Nucellar polyembryony is commonly observed in
In Citrus and mango, nucellar cells surrounding the embryo sac divide, protrude into it and develop into additional embryos alongside the zygotic embryo.
The remarkable longevity of seed viability is illustrated by Lupinus arcticus seeds from arctic tundra, which germinated after an estimated

Extremely small, dust-like seeds, which aid wide dispersal, are seen in
Some seeds are extremely small and dust-like, as in orchids, Orobanche, Striga and Ficus, which helps in wide dispersal, one of the advantages seeds give angiosperms…
A typical seed consists of the seed coat, cotyledon(s) and the
A seed consists of a seed coat, cotyledon(s) and an embryonal axis; the pericarp, by contrast, is the fruit wall developed from the ovary wall, not part of the seed…
The reserve food required to nourish the developing embryo sac within an ovule is chiefly stored in the
The nucellus, enclosed within the integuments, has abundant reserve food and houses the embryo sac; this reserve food nourishes the developing female gametophyte.
An ovary that develops from several carpels fused together into a single structure would be classified as

Which cell of the mature embryo sac is directly involved in triple fusion?
The central cell, via its two polar nuclei
In triple fusion, a male gamete fuses with the two polar nuclei that lie together in the central cell, forming the triploid primary endosperm nucleus.

In a dicot seedling, the part of the embryonal axis that lies below the level of cotyledon attachment and terminates in the radicle is the
The hypocotyl is the portion of the embryonal axis below the level of attachment of the cotyledons; it terminates in the radicle, which is covered by a root cap.

The androecium of a flower is made up of
The androecium is the male reproductive whorl and consists of stamens, each stamen having a filament and an anther; the gynoecium consists of pistils.
The sporogenous tissue of a microsporangium is located
in the centre of the microsporangium
between the endothecium and the middle layers
A compact homogeneous mass of sporogenous cells occupies the centre of each microsporangium, surrounded by the four wall layers.
Germ pores of a pollen grain are regions where
both intine and exine are absent

The small opening in the integuments of the ovule through which the pollen tube usually enters is the
The integuments encircle the nucellus except at the tip, where a small opening called the micropyle is left; the pollen tube enters the ovule through it.

Antipodal cells of the embryo sac are situated at the
lateral side of the central cell
Three cells are grouped together at the chalazal end and are called the antipodal cells; the three cells at the micropylar end form the egg apparatus.

All the events from the deposition of pollen on the stigma up to the entry of the pollen tube into the ovule are collectively called

The primary endosperm nucleus of an angiosperm is
It is formed by the fusion of one haploid male gamete with the two haploid polar nuclei, so it is triploid (3n).
In a grass embryo, the sheath that encloses the radicle and the root cap is the
The coleorrhiza is the undifferentiated sheath covering the radicle and root cap, whereas the coleoptile is the hollow sheath enclosing the shoot apex and leaf primordia.
Seedless bananas are produced as a result of
In parthenocarpy the ovary develops into a fruit without fertilisation, so no ovules mature into seeds. It can also be induced artificially with growth hormones.
The additional embryos formed from nucellar cells in a Citrus seed are
genetically identical to the mother plant

A typical angiosperm anther is bilobed, with each lobe carrying how many microsporangia?
Each lobe (theca) of a bilobed anther carries two microsporangia at its corners, running longitudinally, giving four microsporangia in the whole anther.
A pollen grain measures roughly how many micrometres in diameter?
A pollen grain is generally spherical and measures about 25-50 micrometres in diameter, small enough to be invisible to the naked eye but visible under a microscope.
How many protective integuments typically cover an angiosperm ovule?
The ovule is covered by one or two protective integuments, which enclose it except at a small opening at the tip, the micropyle.
The mature embryo sac has how many total nuclei?

Floral rewards offered to a pollinating animal typically include nectar and
Nectar and pollen grains are the two chief floral rewards offered to a pollinator; in some plants the reward instead is a safe place to lay eggs, as in Amorphophallus.
Pollen-pistil recognition is fundamentally based on a dialogue between
chemical components of pollen and pistil
the colour of pollen and stigma
the size of pollen and the width of the style
the temperature of the anther and the ovary

How many nuclei are involved in triple fusion?
Triple fusion involves three nuclei: one male gamete and the two polar nuclei of the central cell, together forming the triploid primary endosperm nucleus.
The tough, protective seed coat of a mature seed develops from the

The wall layer of the microsporangium that supplies nutrition to the developing pollen grains is the
The tapetum is the innermost wall layer of the microsporangium; its densely cytoplasmic, often multinucleate cells nourish the developing pollen grains.
A stamen consists of a filament and a terminal
A stamen has two parts: a filament and a terminal anther; the anther is the site of pollen production, while stigma, style and ovary belong to the pistil, not the stamen.
In a typical dithecous anther, the total number of microsporangia present is
A dithecous anther has two thecae, and each theca carries two microsporangia at its corners, giving four microsporangia in total.
binucleate or multinucleate with dense cytoplasm
Tapetal cells are highly specialised, with dense cytoplasm and usually more than one nucleus, a sign of their intense nutritive activity.
The inner layer of the pollen wall, made of cellulose and pectin, is the
The intine is the thin, continuous inner layer of the pollen wall, composed of cellulose and pectin, unlike the hard, sporopollenin-based exine.

Pollen of Parthenium (carrot grass) causes allergies and respiratory disorders such as asthma and bronchitis in sensitive people.

The basal part of an ovule, lying opposite the micropylar end, is the
The chalaza is the basal part of the ovule, lying opposite the micropylar end.
The number of ovules found in the ovary of papaya or watermelon is best described as
The number of ovules in an ovary may be one, as in wheat, paddy and mango, to many, as in papaya, watermelon and orchids.
A flower whose gynoecium is made up of a single pistil is termed
A flower with a single pistil is monocarpellary; with more than one pistil it is multicarpellary, which may be syncarpous (fused) or apocarpous (free).
The megaspore mother cell undergoes meiosis to ultimately form a tetrad of how many haploid megaspores?
The megaspore mother cell undergoes meiosis, passing through a dyad stage, to form a megaspore tetrad of four haploid megaspores.
The three cells grouped at the micropylar end of a mature embryo sac, apart from the egg cell, are the
The egg apparatus at the micropylar end consists of two synergids and one egg cell; the two synergids together with the egg cell make up this group of three.
Cellularisation of the free-nuclear embryo sac occurs after the
After the free-nuclear divisions produce a 2-, then 4-, then 8-nucleate embryo sac, cellularisation follows, laying down cell walls around six of the eight nuclei.
The special thickenings at the micropylar tip of the synergids are collectively called the
The synergids bear special cellular thickenings at the micropylar tip called the filiform apparatus, which plays a key role in guiding the pollen tube into the synergid.
The mature embryo sac of a typical angiosperm is described as 7-celled but how many-nucleate?

Continued self-pollination over generations chiefly leads to
Continued self-pollination causes inbreeding depression, so many plants have evolved outbreeding devices to discourage autogamy and encourage cross-pollination.
The reward offered by Amorphophallus, the tallest flower, to its pollinator is
a safe place to lay eggs

How many kinds of flowers, chasmogamous and cleistogamous, are typically borne on plants such as Viola and Oxalis?
Plants such as Viola, Oxalis and Commelina bear two kinds of flowers: chasmogamous flowers that open normally and cleistogamous flowers that never open.

How many key steps make up artificial hybridisation on a bisexual flower — emasculation, bagging, pollination, re-bagging?
When the female parent is bisexual, artificial hybridisation has four key steps: emasculation, bagging, pollination (dusting the desired pollen), and re-bagging.

How many cotyledons does a typical dicot embryo possess?

Seeds whose reserve food is completely consumed by the embryo during development, such as pea and groundnut, are called

Perisperm is the residual, persistent nucellus seen in some seeds such as black pepper and beet, distinct from the endosperm, which arises after fertilisation.
